caption: ingest_counts.py: 500 rows from five ACOG workbooks, 498 parsed; the dates show the counts are school year Fridays.
select_volume.py: one row per station keeping the highest volume across years, as the assignment asks.
enrich_gis.py and lane_review.py: the city lanes field as a starting point, every station verified against aerials.
capacity.py: the ACOG table; LOS E is the pipeline default (config.CAPACITY_LOS).
wards.py: point in polygon with a 30 m boundary buffer; boundary segments appear in both ward lists.
segment_geometry.py and collisions_assign.py: a centerline clipped between its cross streets, crashes within 30 m assigned to it.
collisions_load.py and collisions_assign.py: every row gets exactly one audit category; method B cross checks method A.
scoring.py: combined = crashes + v/c; ranks by ward with min rank on ties.
qa.py: the reconciliation checks the workbook and the dashboard quote.
forecast/growth.py and backtest.py: pooled rates because single counts are noisy; the back test scores each band against the held out latest count.
forecast/horizon.py: vpd(Y) = vpd_max x (1 + g)^(Y - count year); the year a segment crosses 0.9 is the headline.
scenarios/graph.py and closure.py: a networkx graph of 8,115 centerline edges; a closure's volume moves to the shortest detour.
scenarios/daytype.py: factors relative to the school Friday count; game day adds stadium vehicles routed from the interchanges.
scenarios/speed.py and sites/aleph_sites.py: the count string's speed against the posted limit; the top five intersections get a 3D capture.
